skill.name: nextjs-devtools
skill.description: Use Next.js DevTools MCP workflows to inspect routes, components, build settings, and project configuration from an AI coding assistant.
skill.summary: Inspect and debug Next.js app structure through MCP-based DevTools commands.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The skill has legitimate MCP client behavior, but it includes real external command and network surfaces. The main concerns are shell-based stdio command startup and repeated use of unpinned npx next-devtools-mcp@latest; no prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Stdio transport starts a shell command with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Use an argument vector with shell=False, or restrict stdio commands to a small allowlist of trusted MCP server invocations.

remediation.issue: Examples and startup script run next-devtools-mcp with @latest.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and update it through normal release review instead of resolving the latest version at runtime.

remediation.issue: HTTP transport accepts arbitrary MCP URLs and headers.
remediation.suggestion: Default to localhost, warn before external URLs, and avoid passing sensitive headers unless the endpoint is trusted.

remediation.issue: Documentation encourages command execution without safety notes.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear guidance to run the skill only in trusted Next.js projects and to review MCP server commands before execution.

content.user_title: Inspect Next.js Apps with MCP DevTools
content.value_statement: Next.js projects can be hard to inspect across routes, components, and build settings. This skill connects to MCP DevTools workflows for targeted debugging.
actual_capabilities: Connects to MCP servers over HTTP or stdio.
Lists available MCP tools, resources, and prompts.
Calls named MCP tools with user-provided parameters.
Starts a Next.js DevTools MCP server through the bundled script.
Emits MCP tool schemas as Markdown or JSON.
Documents workflows for route, component, build, and config inspection.
limitations: Requires a Next.js project and a working next-devtools-mcp server.
Does not target general React or non-Next.js projects.
Results depend on the MCP tools exposed by the connected server.
Uses local command execution and optional network access.

use_cases.title: Inspect Application Routes
use_cases.description: List routes, review dynamic segments, and inspect route details before changing navigation or API behavior.

use_cases.title: Review Project Structure
use_cases.description: Map components and configuration across a Next.js app before planning refactors or migrations.

use_cases.title: Debug Build Configuration
use_cases.description: Check build information and Next.js configuration when production behavior differs from local development.

prompt_templates.title: List Project Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to list all routes in my current Next.js project. Summarize pages, app routes, dynamic segments, and API endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the route I name and explain its file location, route type, parameters, and likely dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Build Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the build information and Next.js configuration. Highlight settings that could explain a production-only issue.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Debugging Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect routes, components, build info, and configuration. Then propose a minimal debugging plan with risks and next checks.

output_examples.input: List routes for my Next.js app.
output_examples.output: A route inventory grouped by route type, with notes for dynamic segments and API endpoints.

output_examples.input: Check why my build behaves differently in production.
output: Follow-up checks for stale artifacts or missing build output.

output_examples.input: Show components used in this project.
output_examples.output: A component list grouped by location and likely purpose, based on the MCP server response.

best_practices: Run it from the Next.js project root so route and build data match the app.
Use a pinned and trusted MCP server package version for repeatable results.
Review tool output before applying changes to routing, configuration, or build files.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for non-Next.js React projects.
Do not pass untrusted shell commands to stdio mode.
Do not assume MCP output is complete when the app has not been built.

faq.question: What projects is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for Next.js applications where route, component, build, or configuration inspection is useful.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it modify my app automatically?
faq.answer: No. The bundled client queries MCP tools and prints results. Any code changes require a separate assistant action.

faq.question: Why does it need command execution?
faq.answer: The stdio mode starts a local MCP server command, and the helper script starts the Next.js DevTools MCP server.

faq.question: Can it connect over HTTP?
faq.answer: Yes. The MCP client supports HTTP endpoints, usually for a trusted local MCP server.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review the MCP server command, package version, target URL, and any parameters before running the skill.
